newsitem.title: FRANCE: S&P cuts Credit Local long-term rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P cuts Credit Local long-term rating.

text.p: Rating agency S&P-ADEF said on Monday it lowered its rating on the long-term debt of French bank Credit Local de France and its subsidiaries to AA+ from AAA but modified its outlook on the bank's long-term paper to stable from negative.
"The drop in the rating primarily reflects the strong competition in the market for local authority issues that is squeezing CLF's margins," S&P-ADEF said in a statement.
"In addition, its rapid international expansion and development of activities linked to its core business have substantially increased CLF's risk profile," it said.
But, it added, CLF has a strong position in its domestic market, assets of high quality and a good level of equity.
CLF is held by Dexia France and Dexia Belgium since its alliance with Credit Communal de Belgique, rated AA+/A-1+.
CLF has around 40 percent of the market for local authority issues but faces growing competition in the sector.
The downgrade covers CLF Finance Co, Financement Local et Regional and CLF Municipal Bank Plc.
